market_context.summary: A fourth consecutive down week in the AI complex with one violent two-day bounce on top of it, into still-broken trend. The S&P fell 2.7% last week and the Nasdaq 3.4% into correction — its worst S&P week since April 2025, roughly $2.5T of AI market value gone — then 2026-11-09 delivered SPY +2.37% and QQQ +3.54%. The structure did not repair: SPY (752.69) and QQQ (679.35) are both still below their 20- and 50-day, QQQ 5.7% under its 50-day and 10.95% off its high. IWM (282.51) closed back above its 20-day (277.07), 50-day (281.84) and 200-day (279.09) and is the only one of the three to have reclaimed its trend — a rotation read rather than a beta read, since IWM beat SPY by 4.60 points and QQQ by 10.85 over the last month, earned during the drawdown rather than in the bounce. Rates refused to help: the 10-year sits at 4.86% and rising, TLT was flat (+0.05%) on a +2.4% equity day, so this was risk appetite and not a rate-cut trade. Crypto did not participate at all — BTC +0.11%, ETH -0.36%, SOL -1.26% on the strongest risk session of the quarter. Volatility was crushed (VIXY -13.4%). The single fact everything here is downstream of: the Nasdaq rose 3.54% while NVDA fell 4.27%, leaving the index's largest component 26.6% off its high and 18.4% below its 50-day going into a 2026-11-17 print. The index melted up without its leader. October CPI lands at 08:30 ET today and will reprice the open; CoreWeave reports tonight with its 5-year default insurance above 1,000bp, which makes AI capex a credit story and not only a multiple story. Morgan Stanley's Wilson puts downside at 7100-7300, 3-6% below here, before a year-end rally. Today's bar is therefore raised: favour what the rotation is going to, demand a dated catalyst, and do not pay up.

recommendations.thesis: Small caps are the only major US index ETF to have repaired its trend, and the outperformance was earned during the drawdown rather than in a bounce. Over the last month IWM returned +1.28% while SPY fell 3.32% and QQQ fell more still — IWM beat SPY by 4.60 points and QQQ by 10.85 points, in the same month the Nasdaq fell into a 3.4% weekly decline and a $2.5T AI de-rating. If this were small-cap beta it would have fallen harder, which is exactly what it did over 3m (-3.82 vs SPY) and 6m (-2.80). It did the opposite, so money is moving by mandate rather than by risk appetite. The structure confirms it: IWM closed 282.51, above its 20-day (277.07), 50-day (281.84) and 200-day (279.09), while SPY (752.69) and QQQ (679.35) both remain below their 20- and 50-day, QQQ by 5.7% and 11% off its high. recommendations.key_risk: A rotation out of 40% of the index market cap is not usually a bullish event for the other 60% — if the AI de-rating turns into broad de-risking, small caps have the weaker balance sheets and fall further, and Morgan Stanley’s own downside range of 7100-7300 on the S&P sits 3-6% below Monday’s close. The specific near-term risk is this morning: October CPI prints at 08:30 ET, and with the 10-year already at 4.86% a hot core number hits small caps hardest because they carry more floating-rate debt than large caps. That is the one macro input actively working against this trade and it resolves within hours, which is why the entry waits for it. A failure through 268.80 breaks the 90-day low and the reclaimed-trend premise with it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is simply the fourth week of an AI unwind and IWM is up because it is the funding destination of a temporary de-grossing, not a new leadership regime — one NVDA beat on 11-17 and the money goes straight back. The 6-month relative number is the answer that makes me take the trade anyway: IWM is now ahead of QQQ by 3.77 points over six months, so this is no longer a one-month artifact of a single drawdown. But it is only a partial answer, which is why the position is sized standard rather than high conviction, the entry is a pullback rather than a market order, and the plan explicitly takes profit at the first target into the NVDA print instead of holding for the 90-day high.

The second leg is the sell side turning: bullish share is 33.3% but the change is +23.8 points over four months, the largest improvement in any name I screened today, with revision direction reported as improving. Huntsman is 28.75% off its 90-day high of 13.39 in the trough of a chemicals cycle, and the entry at 8.90-9.15 is the convergence of the 20-day (9.00) and 50-day (9.01). Market cap is roughly $1.65B and average daily dollar volume $29.6M, so a 1.5% position is a small fraction of a day's trade.
recommendations.key_risk: The company is losing money. Trailing twelve-month EPS is negative $0.53 (0.04, 0.00, -0.20, -0.37) and it has beaten consensus in only one of the last four quarters, missing by 42.9% and 100% in the two most recent. That means there is no valuation anchor under this position — I cannot tell you what it is worth on earnings because there are no earnings, so the floor is the cycle turning rather than a multiple, and cyclical troughs routinely last longer than a swing horizon. This is also a sub-$2B cap at a 4.76% ATR: a secondary equity or converts offering to shore up the balance sheet is the most likely way this thesis dies well before the chemicals cycle resolves, and dilution would not be contained by the stop. Position is sized at 1.5% speculative for exactly these reasons.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that insider buying at a loss-making cyclical is the cheapest signal in finance — a CEO buying a million dollars of his own trough-earnings company is both expected and nearly costless to him, and the fact that the stock is now 2.8% below his August purchase is evidence he was early rather than right. That is a fair reading and I will not pretend the earnings record argues otherwise, with one miss of 100% in the June quarter. What makes it worth 1.5% anyway is that the purchase is not the only thing that moved: a 23.8-point improvement in bullish share with revisions turning up is independent of the insider and is the sell side revising the forward numbers, not the trailing ones. The position is sized as a cycle option, not a conviction holding, and the conviction is published as 3 rather than the 4 the evidence count would support.
